issues.legal_issue: A possession application enforcing a tenancy right acquired under a repealed law is treated as a continuation of the earlier proceeding and is decided by the successor authority using the replacement law’s procedure.
material_facts: The landlord obtained an order determining the tenancy under the earlier law before it was repealed.
After the replacement law took effect, the landlord applied for possession under its procedure.
The earlier law provided for a further possession order after the tenancy had been determined.
issues.conclusion: The application was to be treated as one under the earlier law and as a continuation of the proceeding concerning the acquired right. The successor authority was competent to hear it and had to follow the replacement law’s procedure while giving effect to the right already acquired.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 132(2) and 132(3) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Vidarbha Region and Kutch Area) Act, 1958, acquired rights remain enforceable, while proceedings pending at commencement are transferred to the corresponding authority and disposed of under the replacement Act. The court treated the possession application as a continuation of the proceeding under section 19 of the Berar Regulation of Agricultural Leases Act, 1951, following Jayantraj Kanakmal Zambad v. Hari Dagdu. The phrase requiring disposal in accordance with the replacement Act attracts its procedural provisions, not new substantive conditions for instituting proceedings.

rule.if: tenancy_possession_enforcement_proceeding and prior_termination_order and possession_application_after_repeal and right_acquired_before_repeal

predicates.tenancy_possession_enforcement_proceedin: The proceeding concerns a landlord’s application to recover possession from a tenant.
predicates.prior_termination_order: A landlord obtained an order determining the tenancy under the law then in force before that law was repealed.
predicates.possession_application_after_repeal: A landlord applied for possession after the earlier law had been repealed.
predicates.right_acquired_before_repeal: The landlord’s right to seek possession arose before the earlier law was repealed.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession from a tenant on the basis of a right acquired before repeal, the successor authority uses current procedure while giving effect to that preexisting right.

issues.legal_issue: Conditions and restrictions governing termination under a replacement tenancy regime do not apply to a possession proceeding that enforces a tenancy right acquired under the earlier regime.
material_facts: The landlord’s tenancy-termination order was made under the earlier law before the replacement law took effect.
The landlord’s later application sought to enforce the right arising from that earlier order.
The landlord had not terminated the tenancy through the replacement law’s termination procedure.
issues.conclusion: The conditions and restrictions in section 38(3) and (4) did not apply to the application. The successor authority was to deal with it as an application enforcing the right conferred under the earlier law, without applying section 38.
issues.legal_principle: Section 38(1) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Vidarbha Region and Kutch Area) Act, 1958, was prospective. Sections 38(3) and (4) were tied to termination under section 38(1), rather than applying to every tenancy termination. Read with sections 132(2) and 132(3), they did not govern enforcement of a right acquired under the Berar Regulation of Agricultural Leases Act, 1951. The court approved Jayantraj Kanakmal Zambad v. Hari Dagdu on the treatment of the possession application as a continuation of the earlier proceeding.

rule.if: tenancy_possession_enforcement_proceeding and prior_termination_order and right_acquired_before_repeal and termination_predated_replacement_regime

predicates.tenancy_possession_enforcement_proceedin: The proceeding concerns a landlord’s application to recover possession from a tenant.
predicates.prior_termination_order: A landlord obtained an order determining the tenancy under the law then in force.
predicates.right_acquired_before_repeal: The landlord’s right to seek possession arose before the earlier law was repealed.
predicates.termination_predated_replacement_regime: The tenancy was determined before the replacement regime took effect, rather than through its termination procedure.

issues.definition: When a possession proceeding enforces a right acquired through a tenancy determination made before the replacement regime, that regime’s termination conditions and restrictions do not apply.
